subject: Commitment matrix & grace window — template redlines
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Horizon Retail Procurement <procurement@horizonretail.com>
Date: 2025-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Service commitment template review and questions

Connor — thanks for sending over Redwood's standard commitment template and the draft SOW (attached). Procurement and engineering reviewed and we have a few asks before we can approve: 

- Monthly remedy cap: the template lists a monthly cap of 20% of recurring fees. That's higher than we expected. Can Redwood consider a 10% cap or a pro-rata calculation tied to incident duration?
- Latency SLOs: we saw p95 targets but no clear carveouts for scheduled batch windows (our nightly reconciliation and peak catalog ingest). We need explicit carveouts and a clear definition of "burst" vs "system incident."
- Maintenance windows: please confirm whether standard maintenance (planned) will be excluded from remedy calculations and provide the typical weekly/monthly cadence and max length.
- Reporting: we'll need monthly telemetry extracts (p95, p99, incident log).

I'm attaching our latest SOW (Horizon_SOW_v3.pdf). Can you propose concrete language or alternative options that would be acceptable to Redwood? If we can align quickly we'd like to lock commitments ahead of our board sign-off.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Horizon Retail

Attachments: Horizon_SOW_v3.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>
Cc: Horizon Retail Procurement <procurement@horizonretail.com>
Date: 2025-12-01T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Service commitment template review and questions

Hi Olivia — really appreciate the thorough review and the SOW. I pulled together two pragmatic options so we can move this forward without blocking your board timeline: 

Option A (standard+moderation):
- Monthly remedy cap: 15% of recurring fees
- Scheduled maintenance carveout: planned weekly window up to 4 hours (per region) excluded from remedies
- Latency SLOs: p95 250ms, with documented burst windows (up to 30 mins) where p95 may be relaxed if KPI monitoring shows degraded throughput across the cluster
- Reporting: monthly telemetry export (CSV) and an incident summary for each remedy event

Option B (committed-reserve):
- Monthly remedy cap: 10% of recurring fees
- Requires committed reserved capacity (dedicated instance pool) and a modest uplift to the monthly minimum (we can show numbers once we settle compute size)
- Same maintenance carveouts as above, but guaranteed isolation for your critical traffic windows

I've attached a working commitment matrix (redwood_commitment_matrix_v1.xlsx) that maps these options to operational constraints. If Option B looks promising, we can have finance produce the committed pricing addendum.

Next steps: I can loop in our legal and CS leads to draft precise redline language. Would you prefer Option A (faster, no add'l fee) or Option B (lower cap, reserved capacity + fee)? I'm available for a 30-minute call tomorrow or Thursday to align.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_commitment_matrix_v1.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2025-12-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Service commitment template review and questions — action items

Laura / Marissa — forwarding Horizon Retail's asks and the two options I proposed. Please see highlights below and help with language and operational acceptance criteria.

(quoted) -----Original Message-----
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 1 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Service commitment template review and questions
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

- Horizon requests monthly remedy cap reduction to 10% or pro-rata calculation.
- Need explicit latency carveouts for scheduled nightly batch windows and a definition for bursts.
- Confirm maintenance window exclusion and reporting exports.

(Action items)
1) Laura: please draft a short redline for the commitment template addressing "monthly remedy cap" and adding a clause for scheduled maintenance and carveouts. Suggested first pass: include Option A language (15%) and an alternative Option B (10% contingent on committed reserve). Need this by EOD 2025-12-02 so we can share with Horizon.
2) Marissa: please outline operational acceptance criteria and monitoring hooks we would require to verify carveouts (metrics, logging, blackout windows). Can you include expected lead time for provisioning reserved capacity under Option B? Need by 2025-12-03 noon.

I'll consolidate and send a single redline back to Horizon. Thanks — Connor

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Retail Procurement <procurement@horizonretail.com>
Date: 2025-12-03T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commitment matrix & grace window — template redlines

Connor — thanks for moving quickly and for looping in legal/ops. After internal review Horizon prefers Option B (10% monthly cap with committed reserved capacity). A few clarifying notes before we sign: 

- Please ensure the redline explicitly states that scheduled maintenance (up to 4 hours weekly per region) is excluded from remedy computations and that batch windows (defined in the SOW appendix as nightly 02:00–04:30 local) are treated as carveouts when validated by telemetry.
- For latency exceptions during batch windows, we want a clear metric-based trigger (e.g., if p95 degrades only during the defined batch window, it is not a remedy event unless end-to-end customer-impacting errors occur).
- We'll need a short statement on estimated lead time and cost to enable the reserved pool for Option B — please have finance/ops append that to the redline.

If those items are in the redline we can proceed to legal review and sign-off. Let's schedule a 30-minute sign-off call on Friday 2025-12-05 at 10:00 AM PT — happy to confirm.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Horizon Retail
